war.etymology: From Old North French werre and related Germanic forms meaning conflict or strife; not descended from Latin bellum.
war.prefix_suffix: No clear productive prefix or suffix in the modern English form.

bellum.etymology: Latin bellum means war. Its deeper Indo-European history is debated, so no more specific root is asserted here.
bellum.prefix_suffix: No clear productive prefix or suffix in the Latin noun bellum.

guerra.etymology: Romance guerra forms come through Old French/Frankish forms related to conflict; they are not descendants of Latin bellum.
guerra.prefix_suffix: The final -a is part of the noun form; no productive prefix is established in this word.

guerre.etymology: From Old French guerre, ultimately associated with Germanic or Frankish forms for conflict; not from Latin bellum.
guerre.prefix_suffix: No clear productive prefix or suffix in the modern French noun guerre.

house.etymology: From Old English hus through Proto-Germanic *husą; a deeper connection with a Proto-Indo-European root meaning cover or hide is possible but not certain.
house.prefix_suffix: No clear productive prefix or suffix in the modern English form.

water.etymology: From Old English wæter and Proto-Germanic *watōr, related to the reconstructed Indo-European word for water, *wódr̥.
water.prefix_suffix: No clear productive prefix or suffix in the modern English form.

night.etymology: From Old English niht and Proto-Germanic *nahts, related to the widespread Indo-European night-word family.
night.prefix_suffix: No clear productive prefix or suffix in the modern English form.

love.etymology: From Old English lufu through Proto-Germanic *lubō, related to an Indo-European root associated with love, care, or desire.
love.prefix_suffix: No clear productive prefix or suffix in the modern English noun.

fire.etymology: From Old English fȳr through Germanic forms, ultimately related to the reconstructed Indo-European word *péh₂wr̥ for fire.
fire.prefix_suffix: No clear productive prefix or suffix in the modern English form.

father.etymology: From Old English fæder and Proto-Germanic forms, related to the reconstructed Indo-European kinship word *ph₂tḗr.
father.prefix_suffix: No clear productive prefix or suffix in the modern English form.

mother.etymology: From Old English mōdor and Proto-Germanic forms, related to the reconstructed Indo-European kinship word *méh₂tēr.
mother.prefix_suffix: No clear productive prefix or suffix in the modern English form.

friend.etymology: From Old English frēond, a present participle related to the Germanic root for loving or caring; it is related to the wider Germanic friend-word family.
friend.prefix_suffix: The modern form has no clear productive prefix; the ending reflects historical word formation rather than a productive modern suffix.
